previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of COPD, chronic alcohol dependence, tobacco use, and prior trauma, was admitted for alcohol withdrawal and suicidal ideation in the setting of acute intoxication. He reported using alcohol to cope with chronic pain from an old olecranon fracture and recent grief over the loss of his two sons. In the hospital, he was treated for alcohol withdrawal with diazepam and supportive care. A chest X-ray showed recurrent atelectasis but no pneumonia, leading to discontinuation of antibiotics and initiation of inhaled fluticasone for COPD management. Orthopedic surgery for his non-healing elbow fracture was planned but canceled twice—first due to patient refusal and then because he consumed coffee before the procedure. A CT scan of the face revealed only chronic facial fractures with no new injury. His hypertension was re-managed with amlodipine, and he was discharged home with prescriptions for pain, anxiety, and smoking cessation, along with instructions to follow up on his surgical and psychiatric care.
